items.title: 4.3.2 Combining Stack and Graph to perform DFS

source_refs.note: Topic 4.3.2 (PDF 118-120, printed 115-117); Figure 4.13 is replaced by the original diagram with the same tree. Long question 7 (its number is not printed) uses the exercise graph on PDF 125, read from the page image; part (a) is answered here, taking neighbours alphabetically. Recorded.

blocks.text: DFS explores a graph or tree as far as possible along a branch before backtracking, using a stack to keep the nodes still to visit. Example: a tree with root 1; children 2, 3 and 4; 5 and 6 under 2; 7 under 3; 8 and 9 under 4 (Figure 4.13).

blocks.alt: Tree of circles with arrows: 1 at the top points to 2, 3 and 4; 2 points to 5 and 6; 3 points to 7; 4 points to 8 and 9.
blocks.caption: Figure 4.13: Graph Representation of a Tree with Numeric Nodes (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 4.13).
